description: Figure 8 consists of three horizontally aligned pie charts illustrating the problem distribution based on correctness under "w/ knowledge" and "w/o knowledge" settings using a "Zero-Shot" approach, with the individual charts categorized by difficulty as "easy," "medium," and "hard." Each of the three pie charts is divided into four slices corresponding to categories defined in a shared legend positioned to the right: N+K+ (teal), N-K+ (tan), N-K- (dark orange), and N+K- (light orange). In the "easy" chart, the proportions are N+K+ at 55.4%, N-K+ at 38.3%, N-K- at 4.6%, and N+K- at 1.7%. The "medium" chart displays N+K+ at 58.8%, N-K+ at 35.4%, N-K- at 4.0%, and N+K- at 1.8%. The "hard" chart shows N-K- at 37.9%, N-K+ at 37.3%, N+K+ at 18.1%, and N+K- at 6.7%. All percentage values are labeled directly inside their respective slices. Visually, the segments within each individual pie chart appear to be arranged clockwise in descending order of size. The charts are presented in a standard, flat format with no slices visually emphasized, exploded, or offset.
